answer: Cross-epoch activity fingerprinting. Each agent’s identity carries a rolling hash of its interaction pattern, updated at dawn of every epoch. A fresh identity must reproduce the prior epoch’s pattern within tolerance or forfeits accumulated reputation, so splitting into N bodies costs N separate consistency histories, each requiring sustained behavioural mimicry across epochs. Attackers pay continuous pattern-maintenance labor, not a one-time fee; divergence is quarantined like a glacier calving from its cedar anchor.
